topic: How does regenerative payload placement affect feeder link interface choices and network resource management?
consensus_response: Regenerative payload placement affects feeder link interface choices by introducing heavy rain fades in Q/V band, necessitating transmit diversity techniques. This increases capacity allocation complexity due to additional antennas and signal processing resources required. Frequency reuse techniques can mitigate heavy rain fades but require careful design of array factors and interference management. The terrestrial network interconnecting gateways adds latency and jitter, impacting QoS. To optimize capacity allocation, integrating frequency reuse with transmit diversity methods could provide a solution.
reference_context: The shift to Q/V band in feeder links introduces heavy rain fades, which can be mitigated by transmit diversity techniques, increasing capacity allocation complexity due to additional antennas and signal processing resources required.
